issues.title: [BUG] _parse_remote_url fails for SSH remotes with non-git usernames
issues.body:
### Summary
`apm audit --ci --policy org` fails to discover the org policy when the git remote
uses a non-standard SSH username (anything other than `git`).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Have a git remote of the form `<user>@<host>:<org>/<repo>.git` where `<user>` is not `git`
2. Run `apm audit --ci --policy org`

### Expected behaviour
The org and host are extracted correctly and the org policy is discovered from `<org>/.github/apm-policy.yml`.

### Actual behaviour
`_parse_remote_url` returns `None` because it guards with
`if url.startswith("git@")`, so `_auto_discover` returns:
> "Could not determine org from git remote"

### Root cause
In `discovery.py`, `_parse_remote_url` assumes the SSH username is always `git`:
```python
if url.startswith("git@"):
    host_part, path_part = url.split(":", 1)
    host = host_part.replace("git@", "")
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.13.3
 - APM Version: 0.12.2

issues.title: shared/apm.md: drop `|| 'all'` fallback on `target` (gh-aw substitution incompatible with GHA-idiom fallbacks)
issues.body:
## Summary

PR #1184 introduced the pattern `target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }}` in `shared/apm.md`. The `|| 'all'` fallback **defeats gh-aw's compile-time substitution** of `${{ github.aw.import-inputs.* }}`, so consumer-supplied `with: target: copilot` is silently ignored — the lock.yml keeps the unresolved expression and the runtime env var ends up empty (which apm then treats as `all`, triggering `copilot-cowork` install attempts that fail with `requires --global`).

## Reproduction

Consumer workflow:

```yaml
imports:
  - path: shared/apm.md
    with:
      packages: ["org/repo/plugins/foo#v1.0.0"]
      target: copilot   # ← ignored
```

After `gh aw compile` (v0.71.5 and v0.72.0 both reproduce):

```yaml
# lock.yml
- name: APM Install
  uses: microsoft/apm-action@v1.7.2
  with:
    packages: '["org/repo/plugins/foo#v1.0.0"]'           # ← substituted (array, bare expression)
    target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }} # ← NOT substituted
```

## Root cause

gh-aw's substitution regex ([`pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go:922` @ v0.72.0](https://github.com/githubnext/gh-aw/blob/v0.72.0/pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go)):

```go
var importInputsExprRegex = regexp.MustCompile(
    `\$\{\{\s*github\.aw\.import-inputs\.([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?)\s*\}\}`)
```

Matches **only bare** `${{ github.aw.import-inputs.X }}`. The `|| 'all'` inside the brackets makes the regex not match → no substitution → unresolved expression survives into lock.yml → empty env at runtime.

This explains the asymmetry seen in the wild: `AW_APM_PACKAGES: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.packages }}` (bare) gets substituted; `target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }}` (with fallback) does not.

## Why `|| 'all'` is redundant anyway

gh-aw's [`applyImportSchemaDefaultsFromFrontmatter`](https://github.com/githubnext/gh-aw/blob/v0.72.0/pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go#L875) already injects schema-declared defaults into the inputs map **before** substitution. With the schema PR #1184 already added:

```yaml
import-schema:
  target:
    type: string
    default: all
```

…and `target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target }}` (no fallback), the behavior is exactly what `|| 'all'` was meant to express:

| Consumer | After substitution |
|---|---|
| `with: target: copilot` | `target: copilot` |
| `with:` (target omitted) | `target: all` (from schema default) |

## Proposed fix

One-line change in `shared/apm.md`:

```diff
-target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }}
+target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target }}
```

Schema default `all` is already declared by PR #1184, no other change needed. Verified locally against gh-aw v0.72.0: lock.yml then carries the literal substituted value (`target: copilot` when consumer provides it; `target: all` when omitted).

## Evidence

- Smoke run with `|| 'all'` (current shared/apm.md): apm install fails because cowork install needs `--global` — [hackathon-white-pig-8/zava-storefront run 25495022790](https://github.com/hackathon-white-pig-8/zava-storefront/actions/runs/25495022790)
- Smoke run with vendor-patched literal `target: copilot` (proves substitution path is the only blocker): [run 25495232796](https://github.com/hackathon-white-pig-8/zava-storefront/actions/runs/25495232796) — green end-to-end (apm install 11s, agent 7m11s, full pipeline succeeds)
- Local repro that the elegant fix (drop `|| 'all'`) compiles to literal `target: copilot`: confirmed against gh-aw v0.72.0

## Optional parallel fix in gh-aw

Make `importInputsExprRegex` tolerant of GHA-idiom `|| <fallback>` so consumers can keep using the familiar pattern. Happy to file that on `githubnext/gh-aw` separately — but the apm-side fix is sufficient and aligns with intent (schema defaults exist for exactly this purpose; the `||` belt-and-suspenders just made the suspenders cut the belt).

## Bonus: cowork-in-`all` malfunction (separate but related)

While debugging, surfaced what looks like a second upstream bug in apm: when `target=all` is passed, apm attempts to install `copilot-cowork` and fails with `'copilot-cowork' target requires --global`. But [`src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py:202`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py) explicitly documents that `EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS` (incl. `copilot-cowork`) is "NOT included in the `parse_target_arg('all')` expansion" — and indeed `normalize_target_list("all")` returns `{vscode, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini}`, no cowork. So cowork is being enumerated by some other code path. Worth a separate issue — happy to file with the same evidence if useful.

issues.title: apm audit drift: skip-with-info on cache miss instead of failing
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm audit drift` (and `apm audit --ci`) treats a cache miss during install-replay as a check FAILURE rather than a skip.

## Repro

```bash
# Fresh checkout, no cache populated
apm audit --ci --policy ./apm-policy.yml
# => drift check fails with: 'drift replay aborted: cache miss for ...'
# => exit code 1, even though all other checks pass
```

## Why this matters

Consumers wiring `apm audit` into CI commonly want to audit the **as-committed** file state without running `apm install` first (because `apm install` re-deploys upstream files and overwrites any local edits — defeating drift detection on tamper PRs). The natural pattern is:

1. `actions/checkout`
2. install apm CLI
3. `apm audit --ci` against committed files

Today this requires `--no-drift` because the drift check aborts on the cache it can't see. That's a sharp edge — users have to discover the flag the hard way.

## Suggested fix

Treat cache miss as **skip-with-info**, not failure. Print a clear message: `drift skipped: install cache not populated (run 'apm install' first or pass --no-drift)`. Other checks continue.

`content-integrity` already covers the most important threat (any deployed managed file edited post-install) using lockfile `deployed_file_hashes` — and works without cache. Drift's "replay install and diff" is stricter (catches deletions/additions too) but should be opt-in for CI flows that don't pre-install.

## Workaround

Pass `--no-drift` to both `apm audit` invocations. Documented at https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/drift-detection/ but the failure mode is non-obvious from the error message.

## Context

Discovered while wiring an enterprise demo where the audit gate runs against PR contents (no install) so deployed-file tamper is visible. Setup-only + --no-drift + content-integrity is the working combination today.

issues.title: [BUG] Custom MCP registry lookup fails — SimpleRegistryClient uses /v0/ API, official MCP Registry spec is /v0.1/
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

APM's `SimpleRegistryClient` uses the `/v0/` API prefix and a `/v0/servers/search` endpoint that do not exist in the [official MCP Registry API specification](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/generic-registry-api.md). This causes `apm install --mcp` with `--registry` to fail against any registry implementing the official spec.

The official [Generic Registry API](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/generic-registry-api.md) defines all endpoints under `/v0.1/`:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /v0.1/servers` | List all servers (with pagination) |
| `GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions` | List all versions of a server |
| `GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions/{version}` | Get specific version (use `latest`) |

APM's `SimpleRegistryClient` (`src/apm_cli/registry/client.py`) instead calls:

| Method | Endpoint called | Issue |
|--------|----------------|-------|
| `list_servers()` | `GET /v0/servers` | Wrong prefix (`/v0/` vs `/v0.1/`) |
| `search_servers()` | `GET /v0/servers/search?q=...` | Endpoint does not exist in the spec |
| `get_server_info()` | `GET /v0/servers/{id}` | Spec uses `/{serverName}/versions/{version}` |

The [Official Registry API](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/official-registry-api.md) uses a `search` **query parameter** on `GET /v0.1/servers?search=...`, not a separate `/search` endpoint.

**To Reproduce**

1. Deploy an MCP registry implementing the [official spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) (e.g. `https://my-registry.example.com`)
2. Publish a server (e.g. `my-org/my-server`)
3. Verify it exists: `curl "https://my-registry.example.com/v0.1/servers?name=my-org/my-server"` → server found
4. Run: `apm install --mcp my-org/my-server --registry https://my-registry.example.com`
5. See error:
```
[>] Looking up 1 MCP server in registry...
[x] Server(s) not found in registry: my-org/my-server
```

**Expected behavior**

APM should use the `/v0.1/` API prefix and spec-compliant endpoints to resolve servers from any registry implementing the official MCP Registry API. Suggested changes:

1. Use `/v0.1/` prefix instead of `/v0/`
2. Replace `GET /v0/servers/search?q=...` with `GET /v0.1/servers?search=...`
3. Use `GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions/latest` for individual server lookup
4. URL-encode server names in paths (e.g. `my-org%2Fmy-server`)

**Environment:**
- OS: macOS 14.7.3 (23H417)
- APM Version: 0.12.4 (6aceef7)

**Additional context**

- [Generic Registry API Spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/generic-registry-api.md)
- [Official Registry API Spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/official-registry-api.md)

issues.title: Add live e2e smoke install for gitlab.com (generic git host)
issues.body:
## Gap

Generic (non-GitHub, non-ADO) git hosts -- GitLab, Gitea, Gogs, Bitbucket -- are routed through `GenericGitBackend` in `src/apm_cli/deps/host_backends.py`. Coverage today:

- Unit: `tests/unit/deps/test_host_backends.py::TestGenericGitBackend` (URL builders).
- Parse/canonicalize: `tests/integration/test_generic_git_url_install.py` exercises generic URL shapes (string and object form, HTTPS/SSH, `gitlab.com/acme/standards` shape) but does NOT perform a live install against a real gitlab.com repo.

No CI job verifies that `apm install gitlab.com/<org>/<repo>` actually clones, validates, and stamps a real public package.

## Risk

Our code path delegates to git for non-GitHub/ADO hosts (no proprietary API). If `git ls-remote` semantics or URL builders silently drift, every GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket consumer breaks with no test failing. This is a thin but high-blast-radius surface.

## Suggested approach

Add an opt-in `@pytest.mark.live_generic` test that:

1. Reads a known stable public APM-shaped repo from gitlab.com (we can publish a tiny fixture at `gitlab.com/microsoft-apm-fixtures/smoke-pkg` or pick an existing public APM package).
2. Runs `apm install gitlab.com/<that-repo>` end-to-end.
3. Asserts: clone succeeded, package validated, lockfile entry has `host: gitlab.com` and a resolved commit SHA.

Skip by default; gate on a new CI job (nightly or weekly) so a flaky upstream doesn't block PRs.

## Out of scope

Gitea/Gogs/Bitbucket smoke installs (separate follow-ups if appetite). gitlab.com is the dominant non-GitHub host and the highest-leverage signal.

issues.title: [BUG] Codex and Gemini adapters pass self-defined stdio env verbatim, skipping placeholder resolution
issues.body:
## Summary

For self-defined stdio MCP servers declared in `apm.yml`, the **Codex** and **Gemini** adapters write the `env` dict to the target config **verbatim**, bypassing the env-var resolution / substitution pipeline. Placeholder forms `${VAR}`, `${env:VAR}`, and even the legacy `<VAR>` are all passed through as literal strings, which results in the MCP child process receiving e.g. `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN=${ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN}` and failing authentication.

This is the same class of defect as #1222 / #1224 (Claude adapter), but in two additional adapters that PR #1224 does not touch.

## Repro

`packages/common/apm.yml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  mcp:
    - name: bitbucket
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: pnpx
      args: ["@aashari/mcp-server-atlassian-bitbucket@3.1.0"]
      env:
        ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN: "${ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN}"   # also tried <ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN> and ${env:...}
        ATLASSIAN_USER_EMAIL: "user@example.com"
```

```bash
export ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN="real-token-here"
apm install -g ./packages/common -t claude,codex,gemini --force
```

## Expected

`~/.codex/config.toml` `[mcp_servers.bitbucket.env].ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN` should contain the literal token resolved from `os.environ` at install time, consistent with the Copilot adapter and with the documented behavior in `manifest-schema` ("Codex currently resolves only the legacy `<VAR>` placeholder at install time").

## Actual

`~/.codex/config.toml` contains the placeholder verbatim:

```toml
[mcp_servers.bitbucket.env]
ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN = "${ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN}"
ATLASSIAN_USER_EMAIL = "user@example.com"
```

Tested with `<ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN>`, `${ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN}`, `${env:ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN}` — all three are passed through unchanged. Gemini exhibits the same behavior on workspace-scope installs.

## Root Cause

Both adapters short-circuit on `_raw_stdio`, assigning the raw env dict directly without routing through `_resolve_environment_variables`:

**`src/apm_cli/adapters/client/codex.py` (around line 218–225):**

```python
raw = server_info.get("_raw_stdio")
if raw:
    config["command"] = raw["command"]
    config["args"] = [self.normalize_project_arg(arg) for arg in raw["args"]]
    if raw.get("env"):
        config["env"] = raw["env"]   # <-- no substitution; raw dict goes straight in
        self._warn_input_variables(raw["env"], server_info.get("name", ""), "Codex CLI")
    return config
```

**`src/apm_cli/adapters/client/gemini.py` (around line 119–126):** same pattern.

Compare with **`src/apm_cli/adapters/client/copilot.py` (around line 512–530)**, which routes raw stdio env through the resolution pipeline:

```python
raw = server_info.get("_raw_stdio")
if raw:
    config["command"] = raw["command"]
    resolved_env_for_args = {}
    if raw.get("env"):
        resolved_env_for_args = self._resolve_environment_variables(
            raw["env"], env_overrides=env_overrides
        )
        config["env"] = resolved_env_for_args
        self._warn_input_variables(raw["env"], server_info.get("name", ""), "Copilot CLI")
    ...
```

The Cursor adapter (`cursor.py:126`) also calls `_resolve_environment_variables` for the raw stdio path.

The fact that both adapters call `_warn_input_variables(raw["env"], ...)` shows the code already acknowledges that `raw["env"]` may contain placeholders — but the resolution step that would consume those placeholders is never wired in.

## Suggested Fix

Mirror the Copilot/Cursor pattern: route `raw["env"]` through `_resolve_environment_variables` (legacy/literal-resolution mode) so install-time placeholder resolution from `env_overrides` → `os.environ` works for self-defined stdio MCP servers in Codex and Gemini, the same way #1224 fixes it for Claude.

This is independent of #1224's change because Codex and Gemini are separate adapter classes that do not inherit the Copilot raw-stdio path.

## Environment

- APM 0.12.4 (HEAD `0693341` on `main` at time of analysis)
- macOS (Darwin 25.4.0)
- Targets affected: `codex`, `gemini`

## Related

- #1222 — same manifestation in the Claude adapter (in progress)
- #1224 — fix for Claude only (does not touch Codex / Gemini)

issues.title: [BUG] Authentication fails for apm install --update with private Git-Repository, SSH based authentication and SSH-Agent

issues.title: [TEST] Add integration regression trap for *.ghe.com marketplace auth routing
issues.body:
## Context

PR #1292 (closes #1285) fixed `apm install` resolving auth at `github.com` instead of the registered `*.ghe.com` host. The fix is covered by 9 unit tests at the resolver layer, but the end-to-end flow

```
apm install -> resolve_marketplace_plugin -> canonical -> DependencyReference.parse -> AuthResolver -> credential lookup
```

is not exercised by any test in `tests/integration/`. The PR review panel called this out as a `secure-by-default` + `governed-by-policy` test floor: the auth-routing contract for enterprise marketplaces is policy-load-bearing but not machine-verified end-to-end today.

## What's missing

A new integration test under `tests/integration/marketplace/test_ghe_marketplace_install_e2e.py` that:

- Uses a fixture GHE-style marketplace manifest (no real network call required)
- Exercises the full install resolution pipeline including `AuthResolver.resolve_for_dep`
- Asserts the credential context is bound to the registered enterprise host (not `github.com`)
- Covers at minimum: relative source, dict github source with bare repo matching marketplace project, dict github source with host-qualified repo
- Uses the marker-driven `requires_*` discovery pattern per `CONTRIBUTING.md`

## Why not part of PR #1292

Fixture-backed integration tests require marker registration and would inflate the PR's scope substantially. The review panel agreed this is appropriately a follow-up rather than a merge blocker.

## Related

- PR: #1292
- Origin issue: #1285

issues.title: Remove `--marketplace-output` flag in v0.15
issues.body:
# Remove `--marketplace-output` flag in v0.15

## TL;DR

`--marketplace-output` was deprecated in #1281 (silently Claude-only despite the format-agnostic name). Track its removal in v0.15 once the v0.14 replacement surface lands.

## Background

PR #1281 introduced multi-profile marketplace outputs (`claude`, `codex`). The legacy `--marketplace-output PATH` flag was kept for backwards compatibility but now has a scope-narrowing footgun: it overrides only the Claude artifact, not "the marketplace output." The flag's help text was updated to "Marketplace legacy compatibility" but no runtime warning fires today, so CI scripts will silently regress when adopting `outputs: [claude, codex]`.

The new surface designed in #1317 replaces it with format-symmetric affordances:

```bash
# Old
apm pack --marketplace-output ./build/x.json    # silently claude-only

# New (v0.14)
apm pack --output-path claude=./build/x.json    # explicit, format-named
```

## Required before this can land

Depends on #1317 (v0.14 marketplace UX) shipping first:

- [ ] `--output-path <format>=<path>` and `APM_MARKETPLACE_<FORMAT>_PATH` env both available
- [ ] `--marketplace-output` has been emitting a real `logger.warning(...)` for one minor release cycle (v0.14)
- [ ] CHANGELOG migration line published in v0.14 announcing the v0.15 removal

## Removal checklist (v0.15)

- [ ] Drop `--marketplace-output` Click option from `src/apm_cli/commands/pack.py`
- [ ] Remove `marketplace_output` field from `BuildOptions` and the orchestrator wiring
- [ ] Remove auto-translate shim and the deprecation warning
- [ ] Remove all references in:
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/pack.md`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/producer/publish-to-a-marketplace.md`
  - `packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/commands.md`
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under Breaking Changes for v0.15: name the flag, point to `--output-path`
- [ ] Delete unit tests scoped to `--marketplace-output`; the `--output-path` test suite should already cover the replacement contract

## Migration line (for v0.15 release notes)

> `--marketplace-output PATH` was removed. Use `--output-path claude=PATH` (deprecated since v0.14) or set `marketplace.outputs.claude.path` in `apm.yml`. The flag printed a deprecation warning in v0.14; CI scripts that suppressed warnings should be audited.

## Why this is a separate tracker

Keeping the removal as its own issue prevents the v0.14 design issue from sitting open across the deprecation window. It also gives the breaking-change CHANGELOG entry a single durable URL to reference.

## References

- #1281 — multi-profile marketplace outputs (introduced the deprecation)
- #1317 — v0.14 marketplace UX issue (defines the replacement surface)

issues.title: [BUG] `targets:` in apm.yml is not respected for MCP server installation
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`targets:` in `apm.yml` acts as a whitelist for skill file deployment, but MCP server installation ignores it entirely and configures all auto-detected runtimes. This inconsistency means users who explicitly restrict their target set still have MCP servers pushed to unintended runtimes.

**To Reproduce**

1. Set `targets: [claude]` in `apm.yml`
2. Add a skill dependency that includes an MCP server (e.g. `yusukebe/hono-skill`)
3. Run `apm install`

**Expected behavior**

`targets: [claude]` should restrict MCP server installation to Claude only, consistent with how it restricts skill deployment.

**Environment:**

 - OS: macOS 15.4
 - Python Version: [e.g. 3.12.x]
 - APM Version: [e.g. 0.13.x]
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): [e.g. 1.80.0]

**Logs**

Skills are correctly deployed to Claude only, but MCP server installation targets all detected runtimes regardless of `targets:`:

```
[i] Targets: claude  (source: apm.yml)
  |-- Skill integrated -> .claude/skills/          ← respects targets:
...
+- Configuring for Copilot, Codex, Vscode, Claude... ← ignores targets:
```

**Additional context**

There are two independent defects causing this behavior:

**1. Singular/plural key mismatch for project-scoped runtimes (`codex`, `claude`)**

`_gate_project_scoped_runtimes` in `src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_integrator.py:973` reads the raw config key directly:

```python
config_target = explicit_target or (apm_config.get("target") if apm_config else None)
```

`"target"` (singular) returns `None` when `targets:` (plural — the canonical form per `apm_cli.core.apm_yml`) is used. As a result `active_targets()` falls back to directory auto-detection and the gating has no effect. `parse_targets_field()` in `apm_cli.core.apm_yml` already handles both keys correctly but is not called here.

**2. Non-project-scoped runtimes are never gated**

`_PROJECT_SCOPED_RUNTIMES` contains only `codex` and `claude`. `Copilot` and `VSCode` are outside this set, so `_gate_project_scoped_runtimes` never evaluates them — they are configured whenever their binary or directory is detected, regardless of `targets:`.

Both defects need to be addressed to make `targets:` a reliable whitelist for MCP installation.

issues.title: [FEATURE] add --deploy-only one-shot artifact deployment
issues.body:
# feat(install): add --deploy-only one-shot artifact deployment

## Problem

There is no way to deploy a single artifact into IDE/runtime folders without converting the current directory into an APM-managed dependency project. Running `apm install <artifact>` always creates `apm.yml`, lockfiles, `apm_modules/`, and `.gitignore` entries — even when the user only wants a one-shot deployment (e.g., dropping a skill or agent into a project without tracking it as a dependency).

## Proposed Feature

Add `apm install --deploy-only <artifact>` — a one-shot deployment mode that deploys artifacts to the same IDE/runtime artifact folders as normal install, but suppresses all APM project dependency state writes.

### Behavior

| Aspect | Normal Install | Deploy-Only Install |
|--------|---------------|---------------------|
| Artifact resolution | ✅ Same resolver, auth, policy, transport | ✅ Same |
| Primitive deployment (skills, agents, commands, prompts, hooks, links) | → `apm_modules/` | → actual IDE/runtime folders |
| MCP runtime config | ✅ Written + lockfile ownership | ✅ Written, lockfile ownership skipped |
| `apm.yml` | Created/updated | Forbidden |
| `apm.lock.yaml` / `apm.lock` | Created/updated | Forbidden |
| `apm_modules/` | Populated | Forbidden |
| `.gitignore` for `apm_modules/` | Updated | Forbidden |
| Target detection (`--runtime`, `--target`) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Requires existing `apm.yml` | Often | No — a directory with no `apm.yml` is valid |

### Critical invariants

1. **Exactly one artifact specifier** — `apm install --deploy-only` rejects zero or multiple specifiers via `click.UsageError` *before* any install side effects (no network calls, no filesystem writes, no config changes).
2. **No silent project conversion** — Running deploy-only in a directory with no `apm.yml` must not create one. Running it in a managed project must not mutate existing dependency state.
3. **MCP runtime config is still written** — `--deploy-only` means "no APM project dependency state", not "no runtime side effects". A deployed MCP artifact requires client config (`.vscode/mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, etc.) to be usable.
4. **Local bundles excluded** — Deploy-only v1 supports remote URLs and marketplace artifacts only. Local bundle paths continue to use `src/apm_cli/install/local_bundle_handler.py`.

### Invocation

```bash
# ✅ Valid — one artifact
apm install --deploy-only https://github.com/acme/review-skill
apm install --deploy-only marketplace:acme/review-skill@latest

# ❌ Rejected — no artifact
apm install --deploy-only

# ❌ Rejected — multiple artifacts
apm install --deploy-only pkg-one pkg-two
```

### Supported artifact types

APM packages with `.apm/` primitives: skills, agents, commands, prompts, instructions, hooks, links, MCP dependencies, and marketplace plugins — all deployed to their resolved runtime targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apm install --deploy-only <artifact>` deploys primitives to actual IDE/runtime folders
- [ ] `--deploy-only` rejects zero or multiple artifact specifiers before any side effects
- [ ] No `apm.yml`, `apm.lock.yaml`, `apm_modules/`, or `.gitignore` entries are created or mutated
- [ ] MCP runtime configuration is written when needed (e.g., `.vscode/mcp.json`)
- [ ] Works in a directory with no existing `apm.yml`
- [ ] Deploy-only staging is cleaned up after deployment
- [ ] Local bundle installs remain unaffected (separate code path)
- [ ] Existing normal install behavior is unchanged (non-regression)
- [ ] Full pytest suite passes (`uv run pytest -q`)

issues.title: [BUG] apm install ignores dependencies.mcp[].registry
issues.body:
## Summary

APM appears to ignore the per-server `registry:` field in `dependencies.mcp` during a normal `apm install` run.

If an MCP dependency is declared in `apm.yml` with a custom registry URL, installation succeeds only when the same URL is also provided through `MCP_REGISTRY_URL` in the environment. Based on the manifest schema and CLI docs, the manifest entry itself should be sufficient.

## Environment

- APM: `0.14.0 (9d1161b)`
- VS Code: `1.120.0`
- macOS: `14.7.3 (23H417)`

## Reproduction

Use an `apm.yml` like this:

```yaml
name: apm-test
version: 1.0.0
dependencies:
  mcp:
    - name: com.example/playwright-mcp
      registry: https://registry.example.com
```

Then run:

```bash
apm install
```

## Actual result

APM does not resolve the MCP servers from `https://registry.example.com` unless this is also set in the shell:

```bash
export MCP_REGISTRY_URL='https://registry.example.com'
```

With the environment variable set, install proceeds.

## Expected result

`apm install` should honor the `registry:` value stored on each `dependencies.mcp[]` entry in `apm.yml`, without requiring `MCP_REGISTRY_URL` to be set externally.

## Why this looks like a bug

The docs and schema imply that a custom registry URL is part of the persisted manifest state:

- `apm install --mcp ... --registry URL` says the URL is **persisted to `apm.yml`**
- the manifest schema documents `dependencies.mcp[].registry` as either:
  - `false` for self-defined servers, or
  - a string custom registry URL

But the code path appears asymmetric:

- `apm install --mcp ... --registry URL` uses `registry_env_override(...)` to export the registry URL for that immediate install flow
- the normal `apm install` path does not appear to apply the per-dependency `registry` value before MCP resolution
- `registry_env_override` usage seems limited to the dedicated `--mcp` command path

That would explain why the same registry works only when duplicated into `MCP_REGISTRY_URL`.

## Impact

This makes `apm.yml` non-self-contained for MCP dependencies hosted in non-default registries. Teams cannot rely on the committed manifest alone; they must also distribute an environment variable out of band.

## Suggested fix

During normal `apm install`, apply the `registry` value from each registry-resolved `MCPDependency` when resolving that server.

Possible approaches:

1. Thread `dep.registry` through the MCP resolution/install pipeline instead of relying on process-global env state
2. If environment-based plumbing is kept temporarily, apply it per dependency when resolving/installing servers from `apm.yml`
3. Add a regression test covering a manifest-declared MCP dependency with `registry: https://registry.example.com` and no `MCP_REGISTRY_URL` env var

issues.title: [PERF] materialize_from_bare does full checkout for subdir deps -- enable sparse-cone (78 MB -> <1 MB, ~10x download)
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm install` / `apm update` cold-cache time for a single subdirectory dep from a large github.com monorepo is ~100x slower than a hand-rolled equivalent. For the user-reported case (`github.com/dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-diag/skills/analyzing-dotnet-performance#main`) APM takes **176.7 s** in the resolve phase alone for a **52 KB target**; a `codeload.github.com` tarball + `tar -x` of the same subdir is **1.62 s, 1.8 MB on the wire**.

The user's hypothesis ("c'est un probleme du cote du repository plutot") is incorrect. The packed clone is ~70 MB, the HEAD tree is ~17 MB, the target subdir is 52 KB. The slowness is in APM.

## Root causes (verified by perf audit; line cites against v0.14.1)

1. **`_try_sparse_checkout` is dead code in install/update.** `SharedCloneCache` is unconditionally attached in `src/apm_cli/install/resolve.py:107`, which routes every subdir dep into `materialize_from_bare`. The legacy sparse fast path at `src/apm_cli/deps/github_downloader.py:963-1027` is only reachable when `shared_clone_cache is None` -- never true in normal flow.
2. **`materialize_from_bare` does a full checkout for every subdir consumer.** `src/apm_cli/deps/bare_cache.py:539-645` runs `git clone --local --shared --no-checkout` then `git checkout HEAD` -- no `sparse-checkout init`, no `--filter=blob:none`. For dotnet/skills this materializes ~78 MB of working tree per consumer per SHA to extract a 52 KB subdir. On-disk `checkouts_v1/<shard>/` accumulates **787 MB for 10 SHAs of one repo**.
3. **No tier-resolver observability.** `TieredRefResolver` collects hit counts at `src/apm_cli/deps/tiered_ref_resolver.py:339` but never logs them, so cold-cache slowness cannot be attributed (L1 commits API? L3 legacy clone fallback?).

## Fix

**Primary**: pass the `subdir_path` from `download_subdirectory_package` down into `materialize_from_bare` (or a new `materialize_subdir_from_bare`) and run sparse-cone in the consumer before `git checkout`:

```
git -C <consumer> sparse-checkout init --cone
git -C <consumer> sparse-checkout set <subdir>
git -C <consumer> checkout HEAD
```

Pure additive. Same git protocol, same auth, same scrubbing. Eliminates the ~78 MB/SHA waste. Estimated 10x speedup on the download phase for any large-repo subdir dep.

**Observability**: log `TieredRefResolver` tier hit counts at the end of resolve in `--verbose` mode.

## Out of scope (separate issues to file)

- `--filter=blob:none` partial clone default
- `codeload.github.com` tarball fast path
- hardlink/reflink into `apm_modules`
- periodic `git gc` on bare caches
- deletion of unreachable `_try_sparse_checkout`

## Empirical target

After fix, `apm install` cold-cache on `github.com/dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-diag/skills/analyzing-dotnet-performance#main` should:
- Reduce `checkouts_v1/<shard>/<sha>/` size from ~78 MB to <1 MB.
- Reduce wall-clock time on the download phase by at least 5x.
- Continue to produce a byte-identical `apm_modules/.../<dep>/` payload (52 KB target).

Full audit report available on request.

issues.title: [BUG] apm install -g hook integration silently broken across claude, cursor, copilot
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

After `apm install -g`, hooks declared in a package's `.apm/hooks/` don't fire on any of the three hook-capable targets. The install log lies in every case: it reports an "integrated" count for writes that did not happen (claude, cursor) or that wrote unusable content (copilot). Users get no signal of failure.

| Target  | Log says                                        | Actual                                  |
|---------|-------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| claude  | `1 hook(s) integrated -> .claude/settings.json` | `~/.claude/settings.json` not modified  |
| cursor  | `1 hook(s) integrated -> .cursor/hooks.json`    | `~/.cursor/hooks.json` not modified     |
| copilot | `1 hook(s) integrated -> .copilot/hooks/`       | File written, but `Stop` event not renamed to `session.shutdown` and `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` left unexpanded |

The canonical source `~/.apm/apm_modules/<pkg>/.apm/hooks/<file>.json` is present after install but never merged into the user-scope harness config.

**To Reproduce**

Package with `.apm/hooks/session-metrics.json`:

```json
{ "Stop": [ { "matcher": "", "hooks": [
  { "type": "command",
    "command": "python3 ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/example.py",
    "timeout": 20000 } ] } ] }
```

```bash
cd ~/.apm
apm install -g --target claude  --force
apm install -g --target cursor  --force
apm install -g --target copilot --force

cat ~/.claude/settings.json     # hooks: {}
cat ~/.cursor/hooks.json        # hooks: {}
cat ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json     # raw Claude payload, ${PLUGIN_ROOT} unresolved
```

Reproduces identically with a GitHub-fetched branch dep (`owner/repo/path#branch`); not specific to local paths.

Also reproduces with the `--runtime <name>` form, with a different log shape:

```
$ apm install -g <pkg> --runtime claude --force
...
|-- 3 hook(s) integrated -> 3 targets
```

i.e. asking for runtime `claude` still produces a `-> 3 targets` summary, and file inspection confirms cursor/copilot were also touched (or attempted).

**Expected**

- claude/cursor: merge into user-scope `settings.json` / `hooks.json`
- copilot: rename event per-target ([Copilot hooks reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration)) and expand `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` before writing

i.e. what project-scope already produces, applied to `target.root_dir` at user scope. The install log should accurately reflect what was written: no "integrated" claim for a file that wasn't modified, a count that reflects declared hooks rather than per-target deliveries, and `--runtime <name>` should restrict deployment to the named runtime.

**Environment**

APM 0.15.0, macOS, Claude Code 4.7, Cursor recent, Copilot CLI >= 1.0.44.

**Additional notes**

- Install logs lie: report success on writes that didn't happen (claude, cursor) or wrote unusable content (copilot). This is the most impactful part of the bug because it eliminates the signal a user would otherwise use to debug.
- `--runtime claude` doesn't filter; log shows `-> 3 targets` and cursor/copilot destination files are still touched.
- `N hook(s) integrated` counts per-target deliveries, not declared hooks. One declared hook is reported as `1 -> <path>` per `--target X` run, or `3 -> 3 targets` from a single `--runtime X` run.

**Related**

- #1485: same shape, instructions primitive
- #1310: claude hooks with unresolved `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (the variable-resolution half is still visible for copilot above)
- #576: scope-awareness gaps; #576 noted no integration tests cover user-scope install->file deployment
- #565: copilot path regression. **Not** reproducing here (correctly lands at `~/.copilot/hooks/`), noted for completeness

issues.title: marketplace.packages[].source: generalize beyond `host/owner/repo` (deeply-nested GitLab subgroups, arbitrary git hosts)
issues.body:
## Summary

PR #1288 (merged) extended `marketplace.packages[].source` to accept `<host.tld>/<owner>/<repo>` and `https://<host.tld>/<owner>/<repo>[.git]`. That unblocks GitHub Enterprise and shallow GitLab layouts, but the regex pins exactly **three** path segments (host + owner + repo), and the test suite explicitly rejects 4+ segments (`test_four_segment_path_rejected`).

Self-hosted GitLab deployments commonly nest projects under multiple subgroups, e.g.:

```
gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects/my-package
```

That's host + 4 path segments + repo. With the post-#1288 schema there is still no `source` form that names this repo — the schema rejects every URL form, the `git: { url: ... }` object form is rejected as "must be a non-empty string", and the bare `<owner>/<repo>` shorthand silently routes to **github.com** regardless of `marketplace.owner.url`. The `apm view` resolver, by contrast, already handles arbitrary-depth host-prefixed paths correctly — so this is a marketplace-schema gap, not a resolver-capability gap.

## Repro

`apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: test-mp
version: 0.1.0
description: repro
marketplace:
  owner:
    name: my-group
    url: https://gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects
  outputs:
    claude: {}
  build:
    tagPattern: "v{version}"
  packages:
    - name: my-package
      description: deeply nested repo
      source: gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects/my-package
      version: "^0.1.0"
```

```
$ apm marketplace check
[x] marketplace config error: 'packages[0].source' must be one of
    '<owner>/<repo>', '<host.tld>/<owner>/<repo>',
    'https://<host.tld>/<owner>/<repo>[.git]', or './<path>',
    got 'gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects/my-package'
```

The object form sometimes recommended in authoring guides also fails:

```yaml
      source:
        git: https://gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects/my-package.git
```

```
[x] marketplace config error: 'packages[0].source' must be a non-empty string
```

## Evidence the resolver itself isn't the blocker

```
$ apm view gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects/my-package versions
Available versions:
  v0.1.0    tag      5d908cad
  main      branch   5d908cad
```

## Evidence `marketplace.owner.url` is unused at resolution time

With:

```yaml
marketplace:
  owner:
    url: https://gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects
  packages:
    - source: my-group/my-package          # the only schema-accepted shorthand
```

I wrapped `git` on `PATH` to log every invocation. `apm marketplace check` ran:

```
git ls-remote --tags --heads https://github.com/my-group/my-package.git
```

The shorthand routed to **github.com**, ignoring `owner.url`. That's consistent with the schema docs (§7.3): `owner.url` is documented as *"Owner homepage"* — descriptive metadata, not a resolution input.

## Why this matters

Self-hosted GitLab with subgroup nesting is the canonical enterprise pattern in many orgs. Until the schema accepts a form that names these repos, APM marketplaces can't list them — and the only schema-accepted shorthand silently exfiltrates the lookup to github.com under whatever auth happens to be in scope, which is also a small footgun for anyone publishing a marketplace from an enterprise tenant.

## Suggested directions

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

### Option A (preferred): a marketplace-level git base, packages name themselves relative to it

This is the shape every other package manager has converged on — `npm`'s `registry`, `cargo`'s `[registries]`, Maven's `<repositories>`. Declare the host/path once, then entries don't repeat it. It sidesteps the "how many slashes" parser problem entirely.

A new field is cleaner than repurposing `owner.url` (which is documented as "Owner homepage" and the official example, `https://github.com/contoso`, is a profile page with no git semantics):

```yaml
marketplace:
  sourceBase: https://gitlab.example.com/group/sub-group/team/projects
  owner:
    name: my-group
    url: https://gitlab.example.com/groups/group/sub-group/team/projects   # still a homepage
  packages:
    - name: my-package
      source: my-package                             # → sourceBase + my-package

    - name: external
      source: github.com/some-org/external           # #1288's host-prefixed form
                                                      # overrides sourceBase
```

Properties:
- Mixed-host marketplaces still work — #1288's `host.tld/owner/repo` form is the per-package escape hatch.
- The marketplace stays portable: forking/relocating means changing one line, not every entry.
- `sourceBase` is a strict prefix concatenation (no segment counting), so it composes with arbitrary GitLab subgroup depth, Bitbucket workspaces, Gitea orgs, etc.
- Validation: require `https://` scheme, reject userinfo / port / query / fragment (same security posture as #1288).

(Field name `sourceBase` is illustrative — `host`, `defaultHost`, `registry`, etc. are all reasonable.)

### Option B (mechanical fallback): widen the source regex to accept `>3` path segments

Treat the last two slash-separated segments as `owner/repo`, everything before as `host + group path`. Same security guards from #1288 (no userinfo, no port, no query, https-only for URL form). Less elegant than Option A but a smaller diff if `sourceBase` is too big a change to land soon.

These compose well — Option A is the principled fix, Option B is available for one-off packages that don't fit the marketplace's base.

## Decision needed from maintainers

Before anyone invests in implementation, it would help to know which direction lands cleanly with your design intent for the marketplace block:

- **Option A only** — introduce a marketplace-level base field; keep the source regex as-is.
- **Option B only** — widen the source regex to arbitrary depth; don't introduce a new field.
- **Both** — Option A as the primary path, Option B as the per-package escape hatch (my read of the trade-offs, but happy to be redirected).
- **Neither / different shape** — there's a direction we haven't considered.

Once a direction is chosen I'm happy to take a stab at the implementation PR (schema + tests + docs), tested against an actual deeply-nested self-hosted GitLab on our side. Just need the maintainer steer first to avoid building the wrong thing.

## Out of scope (suggested for separate issues)

- SSH SCP form (`git@host:path`) — explicitly rejected by #1288 for confused-deputy reasons; not asking to revisit here.
- Non-`https` URL schemes — same.
- Per-host auth wiring beyond what #1288 already added.

## References

- #1288 (merged 2026-05-26) — adds 3-segment `host.tld/owner/repo` form; pins the limit via `test_four_segment_path_rejected`.
- #1472 — handles arbitrary GitLab subgroup depth on the *install* side via Artifactory probe. Different surface, but informs how the marketplace schema could think about depth.
- #1195 (closed) — earlier GitLab host support pass.
- #676, #692 — adjacent source-shape parity work.

issues.title: apm install: redundant project-tree walks (5s on awd-cli, 5 min on TypeScript, 35 min worst case)
issues.body:
# `apm install` does N redundant project-tree walks per run; breaks installs on monorepos > 20k files

## Headline numbers (measured, not estimated)

| Scenario                                       | Files visited | N_walks | Wall time | Integrate % |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------|---------|-----------|-------------|
| awd-cli (this repo), 1 target                  | 1,926         | 27      | **5.0 s** | 74%         |
| awd-cli + 7 targets (Breadth cell)             | 1,926         | 35      | **19.7 s**| ~95%        |
| awd-cli + 20 local-path deps (Volume cell)     | 1,926         | 189     | **5.5 s** | 71%         |
| kubernetes/kubernetes, 1 target (Atlas cell)   | ~29,549       | 48      | **205 s** | 98.6%       |
| microsoft/TypeScript, 1 target (Atlas cell)    | ~81,000       | 48      | **297 s** | 99.2%       |
| TypeScript + 7 targets (extrapolated)          | ~81,000       | ~336    | **~35 min** | >99%      |

APM is unusable on any consumer monorepo above ~20k files today; multi-target install pushes that ceiling lower.

## Root cause

The `integrate` phase walks the consumer project tree once per `(integrator, package)` pair. With 3 integrators (agents, instructions, prompts/skills), the formula is exactly:

```
N_walks = 3 * N_targets * (N_packages + 1)
```

Confirmed by the Volume cell (`find_primitive_files == 9 * (N_packages + 1)`, R^2 = 1.000 at N = 2, 5, 10, 20) and the Breadth cell (T=1 -> 9 walks, T=5 -> 30, T=7 -> 35). Every walk re-scans the same root tree.

Inside each walk, `portable_relpath(file_path, base_path)` calls `Path.resolve()` on BOTH arguments per file. Atlas measured 1.23 M calls on TypeScript, generating ~10.7 M `lstat` syscalls just from path resolution.

`DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS` is missing `vendor`, `staging`, `third_party`, `Pods`, `bower_components`, `jspm_packages`. On kubernetes/kubernetes, `vendor/` alone accounts for **63.6 %** of `scandir` calls in every walk.

## Diagnostic playbook check (from `performance-expert.agent.md`)

| Invariant                                                              | Status today          |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| Each unique unit of work performed exactly once per run                | **VIOLATED**          |
| Centralize at the cache layer, not the command                         | Honored               |
| Hash on fetch, never on warm hit (`local_deployed_file_hashes`)        | Honored               |
| Variant the consumer cache key honestly                                | N/A for discovery     |

## Proposed fix stack (single PR)

| # | Change                                                                                                            | Expected impact (TS)   | Confidence |
|---|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|------------|
| 1 | Memoize `discover_primitives(base_dir, exclude_patterns)` per pipeline run; collapses `N_walks` to `N_packages+1` | 297 s -> ~6 s          | Very high  |
| 2 | Drop `Path.resolve()` from `portable_relpath`'s inner loop in `find_primitive_files`; symlink guard already exists at `discovery.py:602` | 6 s -> ~3 s | Very high  |
| 3 | Add `vendor`, `staging`, `third_party`, `Pods`, `bower_components`, `jspm_packages` to `DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS`        | 205 s -> ~130 s (K8s, pre-#1) | High |
| 4 | Granular `--verbose` perf logging: per-(integrator, package) walk count + duration; total walks summary           | Observability         | High       |
| 5 | Opt-in perf scenario harness under `tests/perf/` (PYTEST_PERF=1), NOT on CI                                       | Regression protection | High       |

Stacked, fixes 1+2+3 take TypeScript from **297 s -> ~3 s** and Kubernetes from **205 s -> ~2 s**. Two-orders-of-magnitude win. No cache layout, lockfile schema, or user-visible contract changes.

## Files of interest

- `src/apm_cli/primitives/discovery.py` -- `find_primitive_files`, `_glob_match`
- `src/apm_cli/utils/paths.py` -- `portable_relpath`
- `src/apm_cli/install/services.py:99,433` + `src/apm_cli/integration/base_integrator.py:531` -- callers of `discover_primitives`
- `src/apm_cli/constants.py:41` -- `DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS`

## Footguns documented

1. `vendor`, `staging`, `third_party` not in `DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS` (Atlas section 4).
2. `portable_relpath` re-resolves the base path on every call.
3. `apm_modules` skip only fires at top level; walks **inside** `apm_modules/_local/<pkg>/` bypass it.
4. `.github/` walked every pass (low impact for normal repos; real for CI-heavy monorepos).
5. `_glob_match` recompiles pattern split on every file (67 M `_match` calls on TS).

## Repro

```bash
# Baseline (this repo)
time apm install --verbose

# Stress (any large clone)
git clone --depth=1 --filter=blob:none https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript.git /tmp/ts
cp -R apm.yml apm.lock.yaml packages/ .apm/ /tmp/ts/
cd /tmp/ts && rm -f apm.lock.yaml && time apm install --verbose
```

## Methodology

Three parallel red-team cells (Atlas / Volume / Breadth), each instrumented with wall-time medians, `--verbose` phase breakdowns, and `cProfile` cumulative captures. Synthesis by Chief Performance Engineer persona using `performance-expert.agent.md` playbook. Full data in the originating session.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-05-29
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-29
**APM Version**: 0.16.0 (0252612)
**Commands Inspected**: 22 (plus 1 confirmed non-existent: `apm config list`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 3     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps clean` help text is misleading

- **Command**: `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The one-line CLI help says "Remove all APM dependencies", which implies it modifies `apm.yml` and the lockfile. In reality it only removes the `apm_modules/` directory and leaves `apm.yml` and `apm.lock.yaml` untouched. The official docs page is accurate, but users reading only the help line get the wrong mental model.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps clean --help
  Usage: apm deps clean [OPTIONS]

    Remove all APM dependencies
  ```
  Official docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`): "Remove the entire project `apm_modules/` directory. Does not touch `apm.yml` or `apm.lock.yaml`."
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the help string to: `Remove the apm_modules/ directory (does not modify apm.yml or apm.lock.yaml)`

---

#### `apm mcp install` options not formatted as CLI options

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: Running `apm mcp install --help` shows only `--help` in the Options section. All functional flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) are listed in a plain prose paragraph at the bottom rather than as formatted CLI options. This is inconsistent with every other command in APM, makes the output hard to read, and prevents shell completion from surfacing these flags correctly.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME

    Add an MCP server to apm.yml. Alias for 'apm install --mcp'.
    ...

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) expose the flags as real Click options on `apm mcp install` (preferred for tab-completion), or (b) move the prose into the command's help docstring so it renders above the Options section rather than inside it.

---

#### `packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/commands.md` describes `apm deps clean` as "Clean dependency cache"

- **Command**: `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The apm-usage skill reference file describes `apm deps clean` as "Clean dependency cache". This is inaccurate — `apm deps clean` removes `apm_modules/` (the installed packages tree), not a download/clone cache. The actual cache is managed by `apm cache`. A skill consumer acting on this description may expect wrong behavior.
- **Evidence** (from `packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/commands.md`):
  ```
  | `apm deps clean` | Clean dependency cache | `--dry-run`, `-y` skip confirm |
  ```
  Correct behavior per CLI and official docs: removes the entire `apm_modules/` directory.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the table row to: `| \`apm deps clean\` | Remove the apm_modules/ directory (leaves apm.yml and lockfile intact) | \`--dry-run\`, \`-y\` skip confirm |`

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm config` group lacks a `list` subcommand, inconsistent with other groups

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Every other multi-subcommand group (`apm deps`, `apm mcp`, `apm runtime`) has a `list` subcommand. `apm config` uses `apm config get` (with no argument) to enumerate all keys, but there is no `apm config list`. Running `apm config list` produces: `Error: No such command 'list'.` This pattern mismatch is a minor but real discoverability friction.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Error: No such command 'list'.

  $ apm deps --help    # has: list, tree, info, why, update, clean
  $ apm mcp --help     # has: list, search, show, install
  $ apm runtime --help # has: list, setup, remove, status
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `apm config list` as an alias for `apm config get` (no args), or update help text to explicitly note that `apm config get` (no args) lists all keys.

---

#### `apm deps update` does not mention its relationship to the preferred `apm update`

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `apm install --update` explicitly tells users "(deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan...)". However, `apm deps update --help` has no such note. Users who discover `apm deps update` via `apm deps --help` have no indication that `apm update` exists and is preferred for the same operation.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps update --help
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    Update APM dependencies to latest refs
  ```
  No mention of `apm update` or deprecation guidance.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to `apm deps update`'s help text: "For interactive upgrade planning, prefer 'apm update'. 'apm deps update' is retained for direct package targeting."

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- `apm --help`, `apm --version` — correct, clear, well-structured
- `apm init --help` — consistent flags, deprecation notices present
- `apm install --help` — comprehensive, all flags documented, deprecations noted
- `apm uninstall --help` — clean and consistent
- `apm update --help` — clear, `--yes`/`--dry-run`/`--verbose` all consistent
- `apm compile --help` — comprehensive, `--all` preferred over `--target all` noted
- `apm run --help` — appropriately minimal for experimental command
- `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps why` — all clean
- `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show` — consistent `-v/--verbose` pattern
- `apm config get`, `apm config set` — clean; `apm config unset` correctly listed in `apm config --help`
- `apm runtime --help`, `apm runtime setup --help` — well-structured
- Error handling — all tested error paths produce clean CLI error messages (no stack traces)
- Flag naming — `--dry-run`, `--verbose/-v`, `--yes/-y`, `--global/-g` are consistently named across all commands that support them
- `--help` / `-h` — works on every tested command and subcommand

issues.title: [BUG] or [QUESTION] Local dependencies in shared repository
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
We have one repository for our organisation containing all apm packages:
```
apm/
    _shared/
        .apm/
        apm.yml
    frontend/
        .apm/
        apm.yml # REFERENCES _shared
    backend/
        .apm/
        apm.yml # REFERENCES _shared
```

When installing frontend/ or backend/ into one of our projects, we get an error because it's referencing a package in the same remote repository:

```
Refusing to install local_path dependency './_shared' declared by remote package 'development-backend-dotnet': remote packages cannot reference paths on the consumer filesystem. Publish the dependency as a standalone package and reference it via owner/repo or marketplace handle.
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create two .apm folders (e.g. _shared/ and frontend/)
2. Make sure one apm.yml references the other:
```yml
depdendencies:
  apm:
    - path: ./_shared
```
3. Install the frontend/ folder with `apm install dev.azure.com/org/project/repo/apm/frontend`
4. See the error in the terminal (mentioned above)

**Expected behavior**
I would expect the _shared/ apm package to be installed as well from that same remote repository.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14.3
 - APM Version: 0.16.0
 - GIT Platform: Azure DevOps

**Additional context**
Is this expected behaviour or a bug?  
  
If this is expected behaviour, can there be a section explaining how to achieve a setup like this? Since I can't find a clear explanation for how to set this up (besides using plugins and a complex setup to make this work).

Thanks! :)

issues.title: [BUG] SkillSpector adapter fails without LLM API key -- needs --no-llm support
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The SkillSpector CLI adapter (`src/apm_cli/security/external/skillspector.py`) fails with "SkillSpector output is not valid JSON SARIF" when no LLM API key (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`) is configured. The adapter builds the command without `--no-llm`, and SkillSpector writes its error to stdout (not stderr), which APM tries to parse as SARIF JSON.

**To Reproduce**
1. Install SkillSpector v2.0.0 (`pip install -e .` from github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector)
2. Enable the feature flag: `apm experimental enable external-scanners`
3. Unset all LLM keys: `unset OPENAI_API_KEY NVIDIA_INFERENCE_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
4. Run: `apm audit --external skillspector`
5. See error: `[x] External scanner 'skillspector' failed: SkillSpector output is not valid JSON SARIF`

**Expected behavior**
The adapter should either pass `--no-llm` by default (for headless/CI use) or gracefully handle stdout containing non-JSON content by checking stderr and exit code first.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS (Darwin), also affects Linux
- Python Version: 3.12+
- APM Version: 0.16.1 (post PR #1579 merge)
- SkillSpector Version: 2.0.0

**Logs**
```
[i] Running external scanner: skillspector
[x] External scanner 'skillspector' failed: SkillSpector output is not valid JSON SARIF: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

**Additional context**
- Root cause: `skillspector.py` line 61 builds `[binary, "scan", "--format", "sarif", *targets]` without `--no-llm`
- SkillSpector writing errors to stdout is arguably an upstream bug, but APM should be resilient
- Workaround: generate SARIF separately with `skillspector scan --format sarif --no-llm . > report.sarif` then `apm audit --external sarif --external-sarif report.sarif`
- Found during E2E testing of PR #1579 (external scanners feature)

issues.title: Bug: marketplace and remote subdir installs drop transitive dependencies
issues.body:
We hit two dependency-resolution problems with APM in a monorepo that publishes packages from subdirectories.

Repo used for repro: `cisco-genai/ai-native-maturity-leaderboard`  
Branch/ref: `setup-apm-packages`

The relevant package shape is:

```yaml
# packages/stack-frontend/apm.yml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/web-design-guidelines
    - git: parent
      path: packages/stack-javascript-typescript
  mcp:
    - io.github.ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
```

```yaml
# packages/stack-react/apm.yml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/react-best-practices
    - github/awesome-copilot/skills/javascript-typescript-jest
    - github/awesome-copilot/skills/webapp-testing
    - git: parent
      path: packages/stack-frontend
```

## 1. Marketplace install drops nested dependencies

```bash
apm marketplace add cisco-genai/ai-native-maturity-leaderboard --ref setup-apm-packages --name repro-marketplace

apm install \
  --target claude \
  --trust-transitive-mcp \
  --allow-protocol-fallback \
  --refresh \
  "stack-react@repro-marketplace"
```

On `0.18.0`, install succeeds but:
- output says `Resolved 1 direct dependencies (no transitive)`
- output says `No MCP dependencies found in apm.yml`
- `apm.lock.yaml` contains only `stack-react`
- the installed `apm_modules/.../packages/stack-react/apm.yml` is stripped down to only identity fields (`name`, `version`, `description`, `author`, `license`, `type`)

We see the same thing with `core@repro-marketplace`: the source package has skill dependencies, but the marketplace-installed package does not keep them.

## 2. Direct remote subdir install stops early

```bash
apm install \
  --target claude \
  --trust-transitive-mcp \
  --allow-protocol-fallback \
  --refresh \
  "cisco-genai/ai-native-maturity-leaderboard/packages/stack-react#stack-react-v1.0.0"
```

On `0.14.0`, this installs:
- `stack-react`
- `stack-frontend`
- the direct React skills

But it does not install the next layer from `stack-frontend`:
- `packages/stack-javascript-typescript`
- `vercel-labs/agent-skills/skills/web-design-guidelines`
- `io.github.ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`

On `0.18.0`, this path now also looks broken in a stronger way: it resolves only the top-level package and the installed manifest is stripped similarly to the marketplace case.

## Why this seems wrong
The docs suggest that:
- transitive APM dependencies should flow automatically
- `git: parent` is valid for monorepo sibling references
- `--trust-transitive-mcp` should allow transitive MCP to flow
- marketplace install is the recommended consumer path

## Questions
1. Is the stripped manifest on install expected, or is that a bug?
2. Should the original `stack-react -> stack-frontend -> stack-javascript-typescript` graph have resolved fully?
3. Is there a supported producer shape for monorepo subdir packages where nested `dependencies.apm` and `dependencies.mcp` are preserved?

Happy to put together a minimal repro repo if that helps.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-05
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-05
**APM Version**: 0.18.0 (fef942a)
**Commands Inspected**: 73 (top-level, all core commands, all subcommand groups, all leaf subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 1     |
| Medium   | 5     |
| Low      | 3     |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm doctor` has no reference documentation page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` is a fully-functional CLI command but has no page at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` and is not listed in the reference index table (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`). Every other top-level command has a corresponding doc page. `doctor` is mentioned in the consumer guide (`docs/src/content/docs/guides/operating-installed-context.md`) as a key diagnostic tool, making this omission especially visible.
- **Evidence (CLI output)**:
  ```
  $ apm doctor --help
  Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]

    Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace
    config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero if a critical check
    fails.

  Options:
    -v, --verbose  Show detailed output
    --help         Show this message and exit.
  ```
  ```
  $ ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/ | grep doctor
  (no output -- file does not exist)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` documenting synopsis, description (what checks it runs: git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace config), options (`-v/--verbose`), example output, and exit-code behaviour. Add `doctor` to the reference index table under a suitable phase (e.g., "Inspect and audit" or a new "Utilities" phase).

---

### Medium Severity

#### Reference index table omits 5 documented commands

- **Location**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md` (the phase-by-command table)
- **Problem**: Five commands each have a full doc page but are absent from the index table. A user browsing the reference would never discover them through the table.
- **Evidence**: The following commands have `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/<cmd>.md` pages but do not appear in the index table:
  - `apm find` (`find.md` exists -- "Trace a materialized file back to its contributing package(s)")
  - `apm lock` (`lock.md` exists -- "Resolve dependencies and write apm.lock.yaml without deploying files")
  - `apm plugin` (`plugin.md` exists -- "Scaffold and manage plugins")
  - `apm self-update` (`self-update.md` exists -- "Update the APM CLI binary itself")
  - `apm publish` (`publish.md` exists -- "Publish a package to a registry")
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the five missing commands to the reference index table under appropriate phases. Suggested placement:
  - `find` -> "Inspect and audit"
  - `lock` -> "Project setup"
  - `plugin` -> "Author and distribute"
  - `self-update` -> new "Utilities" row or existing "Cache and config"
  - `publish` -> "Author and distribute"

---

#### `apm cache clean` has two flags with identical descriptions

- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: Both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes` have the description "Skip confirmation prompt". It is unclear whether they are strict aliases, whether one is a subset of the other, or whether one has additional side effects (e.g., force-removal even when files are in use). The duplication creates confusion for script authors deciding which flag to use.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Usage: apm cache clean [OPTIONS]

    Remove all cached content

  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
    --help       Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: If `-f/--force` is a legacy alias for `-y/--yes`, mark it as such in the description (e.g., "Alias for --yes"). If they differ in behaviour, differentiate the descriptions. Alternatively, remove the duplicate and keep only `-y, --yes` for consistency with the rest of the CLI.

---

#### `apm mcp install --help` does not expose a real Options section

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: Every other command in APM shows individual options in a proper `Options:` block. `apm mcp install --help` only shows `--help` as a real option; the remaining supported flags are crammed into a prose note after the options block. This makes it impossible to discover the flags via `--help` without also reading `apm install --help`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME

    Add an MCP server to apm.yml. Alias for 'apm install --mcp'.
    ...

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either expose the forwarded flags as real Click options (so they appear in the structured `Options:` block), or at minimum format the "Common options" note as a readable table/list. The current inline run-on text is hard to parse.

---

#### `apm prune` lacks `-y/--yes` for non-interactive use

- **Command**: `apm prune`
- **Problem**: `apm prune` removes all APM packages not listed in `apm.yml` -- a destructive operation. It has `--dry-run` but no `-y/--yes` flag to skip the confirmation prompt in CI/scripting contexts. This is inconsistent with other destructive commands in the CLI:
  - `apm deps clean` -- has `-y, --yes`
  - `apm marketplace remove` -- has `-y, --yes`
  - `apm runtime remove` -- has `-y, --yes`
  - `apm experimental reset` -- has `-y, --yes`
  - `apm cache clean` -- has `-y, --yes`
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm prune --help
  Usage: apm prune [OPTIONS]

    Remove APM packages not listed in apm.yml

  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt` to `apm prune` for consistency with the rest of the CLI's destructive command pattern.

---

#### `apm config list` does not exist; bare `apm config` is undiscoverable

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Every other multi-subcommand group in APM (deps, mcp, marketplace, runtime, experimental) provides an explicit `list` subcommand to enumerate its managed items. `apm config` instead uses the bare invocation (`apm config` with no subcommand) to display the configuration table. Running `apm config list` returns an error:
  ```
  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  Users familiar with `apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm experimental list`, etc. will try `apm config list` and get an error. The correct invocation (`apm config` bare) is not surfaced in `apm config --help`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config --help
  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value
  ```
  (No hint that bare `apm config` shows a table, no `list` subcommand.)
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a `list` subcommand as an alias for the bare `apm config` invocation, OR add a note to `apm config --help` describing what the bare invocation does (e.g., "With no subcommand, prints the current configuration table."). The alias approach is more consistent with the rest of the CLI.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm outdated` uses non-standard `-j` short flag for parallelism

- **Command**: `apm outdated`
- **Problem**: `apm outdated --parallel-checks` uses `-j` as a short flag. No other APM command uses `-j` for anything. Other parallelism flags in the CLI (`apm install --parallel-downloads`, `apm update --parallel-downloads`, `apm lock --parallel-downloads`, `apm deps update --parallel-downloads`) do not expose a short flag at all. The `-j` convention (borrowed from `make -j`) is inconsistent within the APM CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm outdated --help
  Options:
    -j, --parallel-checks INTEGER  Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 =
                                   sequential)
  ```
  Compare with: `apm install --parallel-downloads INTEGER` (no `-j`), `apm update --parallel-downloads INTEGER` (no `-j`).
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the `-j` short alias for `--parallel-checks`, keeping only the long form, for consistency with how other parallelism flags are exposed.

---

#### `apm uninstall` lacks `-y/--yes` for non-interactive use

- **Command**: `apm uninstall`
- **Problem**: `apm uninstall` removes packages and their integrated files. It has `--dry-run` but no `-y/--yes` flag to suppress confirmation prompts in scripted/CI contexts. While supplying `PACKAGES...` makes the intent explicit, scripts may still encounter interactive prompts.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm uninstall --help
  Options:
    --dry-run      Show what would be removed without removing
    -v, --verbose  Show detailed removal information
    -g, --global   Remove from user scope (~/.apm/) instead of the current project
    --help         Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt` consistent with other destructive commands.

---

#### `apm deps update` deprecation is not surfaced in parent listing

- **Command**: `apm deps` / `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update` is deprecated in favour of `apm update` (noted prominently in `apm deps update --help` and in the doc page). However, `apm deps --help` lists `update` with no deprecation hint, so users scanning the parent command listing have no indication that this subcommand should be avoided.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps --help
  Commands:
    clean   Remove all APM dependencies
    info    Show detailed package information
    list    List installed APM dependencies
    tree    Show dependency tree structure
    update  Update APM dependencies to latest refs     <-- no deprecation notice
    why     Explain why a package is installed ...
  ```
  Contrast: `apm init --plugin` and `apm init --marketplace` both say `(deprecated)` inline in the help text, establishing that the codebase already uses this pattern for deprecated items.
- **Suggested Fix**: Append `[DEPRECATED: use 'apm update']` to the `update` description in `apm deps --help`, consistent with how deprecated flags are annotated in `apm init`.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **Exit behaviour**: All tested commands return sensible error messages (no tracebacks) on invalid arguments or missing required arguments. Consistent exit codes (`2` for usage errors, `1` for runtime errors).
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every command and subcommand inspected.
- **`--verbose` / `-v`**: Consistent short flag; present on all commands that produce variable-detail output.
- **`--dry-run`**: Consistently named and described across install, uninstall, update, compile, deps clean, prune, pack, publish, marketplace publish/migrate, audit.
- **`--global` / `-g`**: Consistent flag name and description across all commands that support project-vs-user scope.
- **`--target` / `-t`**: Consistent flag name across install, update, compile, deps update, lock, pack.
- **`--force`**: Consistent meaning (overwrite on collision) across install, update, compile, deps update.
- **Deprecated commands properly labelled**: `apm unpack` is clearly marked `[Deprecated]` in usage; `apm init --plugin` and `apm init --marketplace` are marked `(deprecated)` inline; `apm pack --target` is marked `[Deprecated]` inline. Pattern is established and used.
- **`apm mcp list` / `apm mcp search` / `apm mcp show`**: Fully documented, consistent flags.
- **All `apm marketplace` subcommands**: Consistent flags, proper help text.
- **All `apm experimental` subcommands**: Consistent flags, clear descriptions.
- **All `apm runtime` subcommands**: Consistent flags, properly constrained enum values.
- **All `apm cache` subcommands**: Well-structured (except the duplicate flag issue noted above).
- **`apm config get / set / unset`**: Clear argument format, validated inputs documented.
- **`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`**: 29 of the 30 CLI doc pages exist and are well-structured. Only `doctor.md` is missing.

issues.title: [BUG] Marketplace install fails with "Shorthand '@alias' is not supported" when tag_pattern uses @v separator
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Installing any package from a marketplace where tag_pattern uses the @v{version} naming convention fails in APM 0.18.0 with Shorthand '@alias' is not supported. This is a regression introduced by the interaction of two changes in 0.18.0: fix(deps): reject shorthand alias syntax (#1655) and fix(deps): resolve semver ranges against per-package subpath tags (#1658).

When resolving a marketplace package with a semver range constraint, APM constructs an internal shorthand string of the form owner/repo/subpath#pkgname@vX.Y.Z — where @vX.Y.Z is  part of the git tag name embedded in the #ref fragment. The _reject_shorthand_alias guard in reference.py then fires on this internally-generated string because it checks for @ anywhere in the string, without excluding @ that appears inside the #ref fragment.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Set up a marketplace where packages use tag_pattern: pkgname@v{version} in apm.yml (the pattern recommended by APM docs and generated by apm marketplace package add             
  --tag-pattern).
2. Add the marketplace: apm marketplace add owner/repo --name mymarketplace
3. Run: apm install somepackage@mymarketplace
4. See error:                                    

  [*] Validating 1 package...
  [x] owner/repo/packages/somepackage#somepackage@v1.0.1 -- Shorthand '@alias' is not supported in
  'owner/repo/packages/somepackage#somepackage@v1.0.1'. Use object form with 'git:', optional 'path:',
  and 'alias:' fields to install a dependency under a custom directory name.
  All packages failed validation. Nothing to install.

**Expected behavior**
The package installs successfully, as it did in APM 0.17.0. The @v1.0.1 in #somepackage@v1.0.1 is part of the git tag name in the #ref fragment, not an alias.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: any
 - Python Version: any
 - APM Version: 0.18.0

**Logs**
See error above.

**Additional context**
The marketplace.json source format is correct and generated by apm pack itself:
```
  {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "owner/repo",
    "path": "packages/somepackage",
    "ref": "somepackage@v1.0.1",
    "sha": "abc123..."
  }
```

APM 0.18.0 with the semver range fix (#1658) now constructs owner/repo/packages/somepackage#somepackage@v1.0.1 from this object, then immediately rejects it with the guard from  #1655. APM 0.17.0 is unaffected.
